title: Japan Changes Tax-Free Shopping Rules for Tourists
paragraphs: Shopping is one of the main attractions for many visitors to Japan, and tax-free shopping has long been an important part of the experience. However, from November 1, 2026, the way tourists receive tax-free benefits has changed significantly.

Under the previous system, the 10% consumption tax was either removed at the cash register or refunded at a store counter immediately after the purchase. Under the new system, however, tourists pay the full price, including tax, when they buy items. They then receive a refund of the tax only after they leave Japan.

To receive a refund, travelers must complete a procedure at the airport before checking in for their departure flight. This can be done at a customs terminal or through the Visit Japan Web service. If the system shows a green response, travelers can continue to check-in. If it shows a red response, however, their purchases must be inspected by customs officials. After this, travelers claim their refund using the method chosen by each store. Importantly, if several items were bought together, all of them must be taken out of the country, or the whole purchase will lose its eligibility for a refund.

Some rules remain the same. For example, purchases must still total at least 5,000 yen before tax, at the same store on the same day. Nevertheless, several rules have been simplified. The separate categories for general goods, such as clothes and electronics, and consumables, such as food and cosmetics, have been abolished, together with the requirement for consumables to be placed in special sealed bags. In addition, all goods must now be purchased within 90 days of departure.
Some major retailers, such as Don Quijote and BicCamera, have said they will not charge a fee for processing refunds.
Because the new rules have only just come into effect, travelers are advised to check the latest official information from the Japanese government before shopping.
